Class LessonsLearnedDatabase

java.lang.Object
database.LessonsLearnedDatabase
public class LessonsLearnedDatabase extends Object

Title: LessonsLearnedDatabase Class

Description: Stores lessons learned in the same H2 database the supplied Foundations code uses, so lessons persist between separate runs of the application (Contributor story CS-12). It connects to the same jdbc:h2:~/FoundationDatabase the supplied Database class uses and adds one table of its own rather than changing the user table. Each operation uses a PreparedStatement in the same way the supplied register and update methods do, so pasted text can never change the meaning of a query.

The entity classes LessonsLearned and LessonsLearnedList are what the screens call; this class is the only place that knows the table's layout. Create is addLesson, read is getAllLessons and getLessonById, update is updateLesson, and delete is deleteLesson.

    • createTables

      private void createTables() throws SQLException

      Method: void createTables()

      Description: Creates the lessons table if it is not already there, then adds each TP2 column if it is missing.

      The TP2 columns are added with separate ALTER TABLE statements rather than written into the CREATE TABLE, for the reason recorded in Database.createTables in TP1: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS does nothing at all when the table is already there. Anybody who ran HW2 already has a lessonsLearned table with the HW2 columns, and a column written only into the CREATE TABLE would be silently missing for them. ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS is safe to run on every start, so a new database and an HW2 database end up with the same layout and keep their existing lessons.

      That only works for an HW2 table that already used the TP2 column names. Several HW2 solutions used the same table name with different columns (author, body, tags, createdAt). For such a table CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS does nothing, the ALTER statements cannot add description, resolution, or contributor, and every later INSERT and SELECT fails. So, before anything else, a table without a description column is renamed out of the way by moveLegacyTableAside() and a TP2 table is created in its place. The old rows are kept, untouched, in the renamed table.

      Throws:
      SQLException - when the table cannot be created or changed

    • moveLegacyTableAside

      private boolean moveLegacyTableAside() throws SQLException

      Method: boolean moveLegacyTableAside()

      Description: Renames a lessonsLearned table that has no description column to LEGACY_TABLE, so createTables can build the TP2 table under the expected name. The rename is used instead of DROP TABLE so that no lesson written by an earlier version is ever destroyed. If the legacy name is already taken, a numbered name is used instead.

      H2 stores unquoted identifiers in upper case, which is why the INFORMATION_SCHEMA queries compare against LESSONSLEARNED and DESCRIPTION.

      Returns:
      true when a legacy table was found and renamed, false when there was nothing to do
      Throws:
      SQLException - when the schema cannot be read or the table cannot be renamed

      public int addLesson(LessonsLearned lesson)

    • getAllLessons

      public LessonsLearnedList getAllLessons()

      Method: LessonsLearnedList getAllLessons()

      Description: Reads every stored lesson, newest first, into a LessonsLearnedList. The order is by identifier, highest first, because identifiers are assigned in the order lessons are created; ordering by the date text would put HW2 lessons, which have no date, in an arbitrary place.

      Returns:
      a LessonsLearnedList holding every stored lesson, possibly empty

    • updateLesson

      public boolean updateLesson(LessonsLearned lesson)

      Method: boolean updateLesson(LessonsLearned lesson)

      Description: Writes the editable values and the update date back to the lesson's row, matched by identifier. The contributor, the creation date, and the three TP3 attributes are deliberately left out of the SET clause: a contributor's edit has no business changing who wrote the lesson, when it was written, or how staff reviewed it, and leaving them out means no bug in a screen can change them either.

      Parameters:
      lesson - the lesson holding the identifier to match and the new values
      Returns:
      true when a row was updated, false when no lesson had that identifier
